  How to install the stocnet packages, keep them current, and learn

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

This page tells you how to start with social network analysis in R.
You install one package, `{migraph}`, and it gives you all the stocnet packages and their tutorials.

## 1. Install R and RStudio

If you do not have R, install it from [CRAN](https://cloud.r-project.org).
We also recommend [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co),
which make it easier to write and run R code.

## 2. Install migraph

Open the R console and type:

```{r}
install.packages("migraph", dependencies = TRUE)
```

`dependencies = TRUE` also installs the packages that some tutorials need.

## 3. Load migraph

```{r}
library(migraph)
```

This loads these packages:

- `{manynet}`, to make, import, and manipulate network data
- `{autograph}`, to plot networks and results
- `{netrics}`, to measure nodes, ties, and networks
- `{infernet}`, to test and model networks
- `{migraph}`, for the tutorials and the data of *Multimodal Political Networks*

If a newer version of one of these packages is available, `{migraph}` tells you.

## 4. Keep the packages current

To check for newer versions and install them, type:

```{r}
update_versions()
```

Do this before a class, a test, or the submission of a paper.
After the update, restart R.

## 5. Do the tutorials

To see all the tutorials, type:

```{r}
run_tute()
```

To start a tutorial, give its name or a part of its title:

```{r}
run_tute("tutorial0")
run_tute("Centrality")
```

We suggest this sequence:

1. `tutorial0`: Intro to R, if R is new to you
2. `manynet1` and `manynet2`: making and manipulating network data
3. `autograph1`: visualising networks
4. `netrics1` to `netrics4`: centrality, community, position, and topology
5. `infernet1` and `infernet2`: diversity and regression, and diffusion and learning
6. `infernet3`: modelling with ERGMs

To save the code of a tutorial as an R script in your working directory, type:

```{r}
extract_tute("netrics1")
```
